A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have computed all processes that are of order 1 in aH and that are relevant for Higgs boson production in hadronic collisons.

the cross-sections for Higgs production in hadronic collisions is dominated by gluon-gluon fusion, with a cross-section of 0.6 pb for a Higgs boson of mass 100 GeV, and that the cross-section is not very sensitive to the mass of the Higgs bosons.
we have computed all the amplitudes needed for the production of H + 2 jets at the next to leading order.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ggH process is dominant at both energies.
the cross sections for the gg! ggH, qg! qH and qgq! qH processes at p S =14 TeV are 0.4 pb, 0.1 pb and 0.05 pb, respectively.
the cross section for gg! H + 2 jets is about twice as large as the cross section for qg! H + 3 jets.
